item.text: I’ll fix the worker’s restart bookkeeping, store job strings losslessly through SQLite, and let the form submit invalid values to the API for validation. Then I’ll rebuild and check startup again; the previous environment rejected server socket binding, so I’ll report that limitation if it persists.

The restart fix now marks a recovered job to replay its existing attempt, so attempt 3 can finish after a crash instead of being treated as a new transient failure. Input and output are JSON-encoded in dedicated SQLite columns, preserving embedded NULs and lone surrogates. I’m checking those cases against a recovered attempt before the final startup check.

item.text:
Addressed all three findings: recovered jobs replay their interrupted attempt, SQLite stores input and output losslessly, and the form now sends invalid submissions to API validation.

The build and a targeted recovery/string-preservation check pass; the worker starts and shuts down cleanly. The server and smoke/contract checks remain unverified because this environment rejects local socket binding with `EPERM`.
